coordination.duplicate_avoidance: Current canonical next discriminator CM-DATA was concurrently active: research main already contained a fresh CM-DATA PR #693 receipt. This cycle therefore explored the independent OPEN CM-TERM capability instead of opening a duplicate CM-DATA implementation lane.

observed_anchor: CLAY_MACHINE_WORKSPACE.json keeps CM-TERM OPEN because no canonical Clay argv/env/cwd/stdin/stdout/stderr/PTY value/effect path executes a real Linux process without implicit shell/harness semantics.
hypothesis: A direct argv-vector Linux process primitive can provide the host execution mechanism for CM-TERM while preserving arguments literally and capturing stdout, stderr and exit status without invoking a shell.
counterhypothesis: A process primitive that appears direct may still acquire hidden shell/harness semantics or may be unusable at the canonical Clay boundary because authority, provenance, environment, cwd, stream and PTY contracts are absent.
discriminating_test: Compile a standalone C probe whose parent uses posix_spawn with an explicit argv vector, pipe-backed stdout/stderr capture and waitpid exit capture; compare a normal baseline with one bounded adversarial literal-argument experiment.

unusual_experiment.description: Pass shell metacharacter payloads $(touch /tmp/cmterm-marker) and ;touch /tmp/cmterm-marker, plus an embedded newline and UTF-8 argument, through the explicit posix_spawn argv vector; verify they remain literal and do not create the marker file.

observed_result: The Linux primitive mechanism is supported on this local host: direct argv launch preserved spaces, shell metacharacters, newline and UTF-8 literally; stdout/stderr and exit status were captured; no shell side effect occurred.

grf_collapse.reason: The probe falsifies an implicit-shell requirement for the host mechanism, but does not prove canonical Clay typing, effect authority, provenance, stream/PTY semantics, or accepted-target behavior.

next_falsifier: Select the smallest canonical Clay ProcessSpec/ProcessResult boundary (argv, env, cwd, stdin/stdout/stderr, authority/provenance) and route one direct non-shell executable through checker -> typed/effect IR -> single ClayVM -> Linux adapter; then repeat literal-metacharacter and failure/exit receipts on an accepted Linux target before adding PTY semantics.
